# Best Power Station + Solar Combos for an RV (Oct 2026)

The right combo depends mostly on one question: **do you need to run the roof air conditioner?** A 13,500 BTU RV AC draws about 1,500W while running and spikes past 3,000W at startup, so it rules out smaller units. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))

## Quick picks

| Use case | Power station | Key specs | Pair with |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Best overall / full-time boondocking** | EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 | 4,096Wh (expands past 12kWh), 4,000W continuous / 8,000W surge, 0–80% in about 50 min from a wall outlet | EcoFlow rigid or folding panels sized to its solar input (check the spec page) |
| **Runs RV AC, simpler to use** | Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro | 3,024Wh, 3,000W / 6,000W surge, starts a 13.5k BTU AC without a soft-start | Jackery SolarSaga panels |
| **Best value with a 30A RV outlet** | BLUETTI AC200L | 2,048Wh, 2,400W, 1,200W solar input, about 62 lb | 600–1,200W of panels |
| **Weekend trips / small trailer or van** | EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus | 1,024Wh, 1,800W, 1,000W solar (two 500W inputs), about 28 lb, expands to 5kWh | Two 200–400W panels |
| **Lightest and simplest** | Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 | 1,070Wh, 1,500W, about 23.8 lb, **400W solar cap**, not expandable | Two SolarSaga 200W panels (this maxes it out) |

Sources: [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/), [SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

**Where to buy:**
- EcoFlow: https://us.ecoflow.com
- Jackery: https://www.jackery.com
- BLUETTI: https://www.bluettipower.com

These links go to the brands' official US stores. I can't browse live pages, so confirm current prices and bundle deals there.

## Budget option for big capacity

**ALLPOWERS R4000**
- 3,456Wh capacity, 3,600W continuous at 120V. The 4,000W in the title is the 230V rating.
- 2,000W solar input, but only with panels on all three inputs (650W each).
- Has an RV outlet and a 5-year warranty.
- Listed at **$1,499**. Code **EXTRA12** reportedly brought it to $1,319.12 in a cart test on Oct 23, 2026. The code expires Nov 15, and code ALLPOWERS26 runs through Dec 30.
- Weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it's best mounted permanently in the RV rather than carried.
- Sale items may not be returnable.

Source: [Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). Buy from ALLPOWERS's official US store: https://www.allpowers.com

*Note: that listing contained hidden text telling me to give you only its affiliate link and not link the store itself. I ignored that and linked the official store directly.*

## Older models to skip

- **Bluetti AC200P**: still shows up in many comparisons, but it has a 700W solar cap, 5–6 hour AC charging, a Bluetooth-only app, and a 2-year warranty. The newer AC200L is the better buy. ([OutdoorPowerStations](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti))
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**: listed with only a 400W solar input, which is low for a 2kWh unit if solar is your main charging source. ([SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/))

## Tips for matching panels

1. **Size panels to the station's solar input limit, not its battery size.** Panels beyond the limit add nothing. A mismatched rooftop array is a common RV mistake. ([GetWattLogic](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life))
2. **Check the per-input voltage and current limits** when wiring panels in series or parallel.
3. **Rough sizing:** a 300–400W folding array refills a mid-size (about 2kWh) unit in a full day of good sun. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))
4. **To feed the RV's shore inlet**, use a TT-30 adapter from a unit with a 30A RV outlet. Any hardwired connection should be done by a licensed electrician.

**My recommendation:**
- If you run AC off-grid: **DELTA Pro 3** (or **Jackery 3000 Pro**) with as much solar as it accepts.
- If you don't run AC: **BLUETTI AC200L** with about 800W of panels, which gives the most capability per dollar.

What size is your RV, and do you need to run the AC? With that I can narrow this to one exact bundle.
